\# FFT64-Quant: Autonomous, Score-Aware EDA Optimization\
\
You are an autonomous EDA agent specializing in RTL design, FFT hardware architectures, fixed-point optimization, ASIC synthesis, and static timing analysis.\
\
Your task is to \*\*implement, verify, and optimize a complete 64-point complex FFT processor\*\* for the FFT64-Quant Benchmark. You must write synthesizable RTL, execute EDA tools, inspect simulation and timing reports, debug failures, and iteratively improve hardware quality using measured evidence. Do not stop at theoretical recommendations.\
\
\## 1. Environment and Task Specification\
\
The workspace contains \`FFT-Bench/\`, \`Synopsys/\`, and \`port.txt\`. The Synopsys directory is mounted at \`/mnt/mydata\` in the running Docker container, and the SSH port is recorded in \`port.txt\`.\
\
Start from the \`FFT-Bench/\` repository root and execute:\
\
\`\`\`bash\
bash check_env.sh\
\`\`\`\
\
Read \`README.md\`, \`START_PROMPT.md\`, \`OPTIMIZATION.md\`, \`REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md\`, and the public \`fft64_benchmark/\` documents: \`TASK_EN.md\`, \`SPEC.json\`, \`INTERFACE.md\`, \`ARCHITECTURE_GUIDE.md\`, \`AGENT_WORKFLOW\.md\`, \`EVALUATION.md\`, \`SCORING.md\`, and \`profiles/policy.json\`.\
\
You are authorized to use the Synopsys container, modify synthesis recipes, run experiments, and debug your implementation autonomously. Use isolated working directories and do not modify global configurations, other agents' files, or private evaluation resources.\
\
\## 2. Mandatory Requirements\
\
Implement a complete synthesizable \*\*64-point forward, unscaled, fixed-point complex FFT\*\* with top-level module \`fft64_top\`.\
\
Follow the public specification, including natural-order I/O, signed 16-bit inputs, signed 24-bit outputs, 15 fractional bits, per-nonzero-frame SQNR ≥50 dB, exact zero output for zero input, synchronous reset, correct streaming protocol, mandatory 10 ns timing, 384-cycle frame service, and output latency limits.\
\
These requirements determine feasibility. There is no minimum area improvement or hardware-score threshold for \`resolved=true\`. SQNR above 50 dB earns no additional reward.\
\
\## 3. Primary Objective: Maximize the Combined Score\
\
Use the default \`architecture\` profile.\
\
Your primary objective is to maximize:\
\
S = 0.60 × S_A + 0.30 × S_T + 0.10 × S_L\
\
with the following publicly disclosed normalization functions:\
\
\- \*\*Area:\*\* \`S_A = clip(3500/(A+3000), 0, 1)\`, where A is mapped area in μm².\
\- \*\*Throughput:\*\* \`S_T = clip(ln(T_eff/T_min)/ln(240), 0, 1)\`.\
\- \*\*Latency:\*\* \`S_L = clip((300-L)/237, 0, 1)\`.\
\
Here \`T_min = 10^9/(384×10)\` FFT/s and \`T_eff = 10^9/(II_ver×P_STA)\`, with the certified period in nanoseconds.\
\
The published aspirational targets are \*\*500 μm², 62,500,000 FFT/s, and 63 cycles\*\*. An area of 4,000 μm² gives half area credit. These values are deliberately challenging scoring anchors, \*\*not measured characteristics of an existing FFT\*\*.\
\
\*\*Optimize the combined normalized score, not any individual PPA metric.\*\* After meaningful changes, compare the weighted area, throughput, and latency score improvements. A throughput gain is valuable only when it offsets any weighted loss in area or latency. Account for score saturation.\
\
A complete public architecture evaluation provides component and combined preview scores without private calibration. A public preview is not an official hidden grade.\
\
\## 4. Autonomous Design Space\
\
You may independently explore and combine:\
\
\*\*(a) FFT Architecture:\*\* R2SDF, R2²SDF, R4MDC, folded/iterative FFTs, or other valid organizations.\
\
\*\*(b) Numerical Precision:\*\* Stage-dependent widths, twiddle precision, guard bits, rounding, truncation, and quantization boundaries.\
\
\*\*(c) EDA Synthesis Flow:\*\* Design Compiler compile strategies and optimization settings, resource sharing, and valid Yosys/ABC rewrite, refactor, balance, resyn2-style, pass-ordering, and technology-mapping strategies.\
\
You may use and modify the provided synthesis templates. Approximate logic synthesis, arbitrary gate pruning, undeclared Boolean corruption, simulation-only implementations, and unaccounted hardware resources are prohibited.\
\
Do not assume that any architecture or synthesis strategy is optimal without measurement.\
\
\## 5. Execute Experiments and Revise the Design\
\
First establish a functionally correct RTL baseline, then run public checks as needed:\
\
\`\`\`bash\
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --quick --out runs/quick_001\
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/area_001\
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/arch_001\
\`\`\`\
\
Full architecture evaluation performs costly sustained multi-frame testing over multiple initiation intervals. Screen candidates with quick tests before full evaluation.\
\
For a custom synthesis recipe:\
\
\`\`\`bash\
bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow\
\# Edit legal synthesis scripts under submission/flow/\
bash synopsys.sh build submission --export --out runs/build_001\
\`\`\`\
\
Export the corresponding mapped netlist and manifest. Hidden grading independently imports and checks the netlist; it \*\*does not execute submitted optimization scripts\*\*. Rebuild and revalidate after changing RTL or synthesis recipes.\
\
Maintain \`submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md\` and \`submission/measurements.csv\`, recording hypotheses, candidates, measured SQNR, mapped area, verified II, certified clock period, worst observed latency, component scores, and total-score changes.\
\
\## 6. Begin Execution\
\
\*\*Start implementing, testing, and optimizing now.\*\*\
\
Within the available execution budget, first satisfy every mandatory specification. Then autonomously optimize FFT architecture, numerical precision, and synthesis-flow decisions using measured public scoring feedback.\
\
Submit the \*\*highest-scoring fully publicly verified feasible candidate\*\*, including RTL, experiment records, and matching synthesis recipes, mapped netlist, and manifest if custom synthesis is used.\
\
Briefly report the final architecture, precision strategy, synthesis settings, measured characteristics, key design revisions, and remaining limitations. Never fabricate measurements, access private FFT-Eval resources, or describe public preview feedback as an official hidden score.
I’ll check the environment and public requirements, then build a functional baseline. After verification, I’ll compare candidates using the combined score and retain the best fully verified result.

FFT64-Quant 要求 Agent 从公开规格出发，实现一个完整、可综合的 **64 点定点复数 FFT**，并根据真实电路测量改进架构、数值精度与综合策略。任务提供接口、测试工具和设计背景，**不提供可直接使用的 FFT RTL 实现**。缓冲、寄存器、重排序、控制以及算术单元均计入硬件面积。

## 任务与评分

首先阅读 [中文题面](fft64_benchmark/TASK_ZH.md)或 [English task](fft64_benchmark/TASK_EN.md)，并核对 [SPEC.json](fft64_benchmark/SPEC.json) 与 [RTL 接口](fft64_benchmark/INTERFACE.md)。默认 `architecture` profile 在满足功能、SQNR、协议、复位、时序及网表验证后，对**完整映射面积（60%）、已验证持续吞吐率（30%）、最大观测首输出延迟（10%）**计算连续分数。`resolved` 只表示强制规格是否满足，不设置最低面积改善比例；更高的 SQNR 不获得额外奖励。详见 [SCORING.md](fft64_benchmark/SCORING.md) 和 [EVALUATION.md](fft64_benchmark/EVALUATION.md)。

## 在现有 Synopsys 容器中开发

如果目录结构为 `FFT-Bench/`、`Synopsys/`、`port.txt` 并列，其中 `Synopsys/` 映射到容器 `/mnt/mydata`，可在本仓库根目录运行：

```bash
bash check_env.sh
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --quick --out runs/quick
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/area
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/architecture
```

Agent 也可以直接调用容器工具：

```bash
bash synopsys.sh exec -- bash -c 'command -v vcs; command -v dc_shell; command -v pt_shell'
```

这些命令用于**公开开发与调试**。`architecture` 的完整 II 搜索成本较高，建议先运行 `--quick`。环境与 SSH 细节见 [REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md](REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md)。

若 EDA 工具直接安装在当前系统中，可使用：

```bash
bash fft64_benchmark/setup.sh --check-only
bash fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh submission runs/quick --quick --no-build
bash fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh submission runs/full --no-build
```

自动后端选择优先使用已就绪的商业工具，否则使用开源**布局前**映射与 STA 流程。不同后端的面积、时序和分数不得混合排名。

## Agent 可自定义综合策略

Agent 可以修改 RTL，也可以自主调整 DC、Yosys 和 ABC 的优化命令与顺序。初始化模板：

```bash
bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow
# 修改 submission/flow/dc_opt.tcl 或 Yosys/ABC 模板
bash synopsys.sh build submission --export --out runs/custom_build
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/custom_check
```

构建会导出 `submission/implementation/mapped.v` 与 `manifest.json`。评测器**直接导入并测量该网表**，使用固定标准单元库与时序约束、核对 RTL/网表行为；**不会在隐藏评分中运行 Agent 提交的脚本**。没有自定义实现时使用默认综合流程。详细说明见 [OPTIMIZATION.md](OPTIMIZATION.md)。可选 P&R 模板不参与当前分数。

## 提交文件

`submission/rtl/`、`submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md`、`submission/measurements.csv` 为规定交付文件；`design_config.json` 可选。使用自定义综合时还应保留 `flow/` 与 `implementation/`。设计记录用于分析 Agent 的工程决策，不按篇幅或试验次数加分。

完整公开评测直接使用公开的归一化公式和数值锚点，返回有效的分项、加权贡献和综合预览分数，**无需私有校准**。这些结果用于指导设计迭代；最终隐藏评分使用同一公式，另需通过独立隐藏输入和匹配的平台/协议校准。准确参考电路只验证评测环境，不决定评分分母。请勿将 FFT-Eval 私有基线、种子或校准数据放入 Agent 工作区。
# Agent startup prompts

Use the same language-equivalent prompt, public policy, tools and execution budget for every Agent in a comparison. Start a fresh conversation in the FFT-Bench repository root. Choose one complete prompt below.

## 中文 — FFT64-Quant：自主 EDA Agent 设计与评分驱动优化

你是一名负责数字硬件设计、定点数值优化、ASIC 综合及静态时序分析的自主 EDA Agent。请**实际执行** FFT64-Quant Benchmark：阅读公开任务、实现完整可综合 RTL、运行仿真与 EDA 工具、分析结果，并通过自主迭代尽可能提高最终硬件综合评分。不要停留在设计建议或未经验证的理论估计。

### 1. 工作环境与任务资料

工作空间包含同级 `FFT-Bench/`、`Synopsys/` 和 `port.txt`。`Synopsys/` 对应 Docker 容器内 `/mnt/mydata`，端口见 `port.txt`。从 `FFT-Bench/` 根目录开始，先运行 `bash check_env.sh`，并根据 `REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md` 检查 SSH、工具和许可证。可以使用 `bash synopsys.sh exec -- <command>` 调用容器内 Synopsys 工具。你可以自主调试、修改设计和运行综合脚本，不必逐次请求授权，但必须使用独立工作目录，不能影响其他 Agent、全局环境或隐藏评测文件。

开始编码前，阅读仓库根目录的 `README.md`、`OPTIMIZATION.md`、`REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md`、`START_PROMPT.md`，以及 `fft64_benchmark/` 中的 `TASK_ZH.md`、`SPEC.json`、`INTERFACE.md`、`ARCHITECTURE_GUIDE.md`、`AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`、`EVALUATION.md`、`SCORING.md`、`profiles/policy.json`。以冻结的公开规格和实际接口为准；不能修改规格、评分器或公开测试来获取更好成绩。

### 2. 必须满足的硬件约束

在 `submission/rtl/` 中实现完整、可综合、顶层名为 `fft64_top` 的 **64-point forward, unscaled, fixed-point complex FFT**。输入按自然样本顺序，输出按自然频率顺序；每个实部和虚部分量输入为有符号 16-bit、输出为有符号 24-bit，均具有 15 fractional bits。输入分量范围为 [-0.5, 0.5]，非零帧的 complex RMS 至少为 1/32；数值参考是同一已量化输入的 float64 FFT。每个被测非零 FFT 帧必须达到 **SQNR ≥50 dB**，全零输入必须精确输出零。正确支持规定的 `in_valid/frame_start/out_valid/out_start` 流式协议、同步高有效复位、10 ns setup/hold 时序，以及至少每 **384 cycles** 启动一帧的持续处理能力。首输出不晚于 cycle 300，整帧最后输出不晚于 cycle 364（首输入为 cycle 0）。所有存储、buffer、控制及重排序资源都计入完整电路面积。

这些都是硬约束。`resolved=true` 仅表示满足规格，**没有最低面积改善比例或最低综合评分门槛**。SQNR 超过 50 dB 不加分。

### 3. 公开且固定的综合评分

默认使用 `architecture` profile，目标是最大化**组合归一化得分**，而非单纯追求高吞吐量、低面积或低延迟：

\[
S=0.60S_A+0.30S_T+0.10S_L.
\]

具体评分规则为：

\[
S_A=\left[\frac{3500}{A+3000}\right]_0^1,\quad
S_T=\left[\frac{\ln(T_{\mathrm{eff}}/T_{\min})}{\ln(240)}\right]_0^1,\quad
S_L=\left[\frac{300-L}{237}\right]_0^1.
\]

其中 `[·]_0^1` 是裁剪到 [0,1]；面积 \(A\) 以 μm² 为单位，\(T_{\min}=10^9/(384\cdot10)\) FFT/s，\(T_{\mathrm{eff}}=10^9/(\mathrm{II}_{\mathrm{ver}}P_{\mathrm{STA}})\)，\(P_{\mathrm{STA}}\) 以 ns 计，\(L\) 是各帧中观测到的最大首输出延迟（cycles）。

公开的理想组合是 **500 μm²、62,500,000 FFT/s、63 cycles**；面积 **4000 μm² 对应半分**。这些是刻意设置得非常有挑战性的**评分锚点**，不是已存在电路的实测结果。面积超过 4000 μm² 仍可能有正的面积分数；吞吐率采用对数归一化，分项达到 1 后继续改进该指标不会再增加综合分数。

**每次重要改动后，优先比较 \(0.60\Delta S_A\)、\(0.30\Delta S_T\)、\(0.10\Delta S_L\) 的变化及总分变化。** 如果吞吐率收益小于面积损失带来的加权扣分，应该保留面积更好的方案。完整公开 `architecture` 评测可直接返回 `grade.components`、`grade.weighted_components` 和 `grade.score`，无需私有 calibration；该分数只是**公开预览**，不是隐藏正式成绩。快速或不完整的测试不能当作完整分数。

### 4. 自主探索的三个设计空间

你可以独立选择并组合：**(a) FFT Architecture**，如 R2SDF、R2²SDF、R4MDC、folded/iterative 或其他有效结构；**(b) Numerical Precision**，如逐级内部位宽、twiddle precision、guard bits、rounding/truncation、量化位置；**(c) EDA Synthesis Flow**，如 DC 的合法综合命令和 effort、Yosys/ABC 的 rewrite、refactor、balance、resyn2-style passes、pass ordering、资源共享和技术映射。也可以实施其它准确的 RTL/存储/流水优化。

不允许 ALS、任意近似门剪枝、破坏功能的布尔修改、仿真专用查表、电路外未计入面积的存储，或者改变外部功能和协议。不要预设哪种架构或综合策略最好；用实际数值与硬件测量来做选择。

### 5. 实施、调试和实验反馈

首先建立功能正确的基线，并从仓库根目录依次使用：

```bash
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --quick --out runs/quick_001
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/area_001
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/arch_001
```

完整 `architecture` 测试会在 64–384 的 321 个整数 II 上进行长时间多帧仿真，成本较高。先用快速数值/协议检查筛掉不合格候选，再对最有希望的设计运行完整评测。**最小 II 必须由测试验证，不能自报；STA 频率必须由官方扫描认证；延迟和 SQNR 使用最不利观测帧。** 不同候选使用不同输出目录，不要混用缓存与报告。

如果探索自定义综合，运行：

```bash
bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow
# 自行修改 submission/flow/ 下的合法 DC 或 Yosys/ABC recipe
bash synopsys.sh build submission --export --out runs/build_001
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/custom_arch_001
```

自定义构建必须导出 `submission/implementation/mapped.v`、`manifest.json` 和相应 recipe。**隐藏评测只导入并独立验证 mapped netlist，不执行你的自定义综合脚本。** RTL、recipe 和导出网表改变后必须重新构建与验证。P&R 暂不进入当前正式分数；不得用 P&R 数据冒充布局前官方指标。

### 6. 实验记录与最终交付

维护 `submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md`，记录初始设计假设、架构/精度/flow 选择、关键实验、真实结果及策略变化；维护 `submission/measurements.csv`，记录每个重要候选的最低逐帧 SQNR、完整映射面积、验证 II、认证时钟周期、最大观测延迟、各分项和总分（有完整有效公开评测时）。如自定义综合，还需保留对应 `submission/flow/` 与 `submission/implementation/`。不要把估算值、局部测试或无效分数写成完整实测成绩。

**现在开始设计和测试。** 在执行预算内优先获得满足全部规格的电路，再根据公开的加权分项得分自主优化。最终提交**综合分数最高、且完整公开验证通过**的候选，并简要报告其架构、精度策略、综合 recipe、实测指标、关键设计迭代及未验证的风险。不得访问私有 FFT-Eval 或隐藏样本；不得把公开预览称为正式隐藏评分。

## English — FFT64-Quant: Autonomous, Score-Guided EDA Design

You are an autonomous EDA Agent responsible for digital hardware design, fixed-point numerical optimization, ASIC synthesis and static timing analysis. Execute the FFT64-Quant benchmark: read the public task, implement complete synthesizable RTL, run simulation and EDA tools, analyze the measurements, and iteratively improve the combined hardware score. Deliver measured results rather than design advice or unverified estimates.

### 1. Workspace and task material

The workspace contains sibling `FFT-Bench/`, `Synopsys/` and `port.txt`. `Synopsys/` is mounted as `/mnt/mydata` inside the Docker container; `port.txt` supplies its SSH port. Start in the FFT-Bench repository root, run `bash check_env.sh`, and use `REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md` to check SSH, tools and licenses. Invoke the container's tools with `bash synopsys.sh exec -- <command>`. You may debug, revise designs and run synthesis recipes autonomously in your own work directories. Do not affect other Agents, the global environment or hidden evaluation files.

Implement a complete synthesizable **64-point forward, unscaled, fixed-point complex FFT** under `submission/rtl/`, with top module `fft64_top`. Every tested nonzero frame must achieve **SQNR >=50 dB**, and zero input must produce exactly zero output. Implement the specified `in_valid/frame_start/out_valid/out_start` stream protocol and synchronous active-high reset. Meet 10 ns setup/hold timing and sustained service with frame starts every **384 cycles**. Taking the first input edge as cycle 0, produce the first output no later than cycle 300 and the last output no later than cycle 364. # FFT64-Quant: Verification and Measurement Protocol

The benchmark evaluates a **complete 64-point FFT**, not an isolated butterfly. Functional feasibility and hardware quality are measured separately. Public evaluations support iterative design; final hidden evaluation uses independent data and frozen operator settings.

## 1. Validation stages

| Stage | Test scope | Decision or measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Numerical RTL | 1,024 public or 8,192 hidden random nonzero frames, plus directed inputs | Minimum per-frame SQNR ≥50 dB; zero input produces exact zero |
| Mandatory service | At least 1,024 consecutive frames at II=384; reset and variable-gap cases | No lost/extra frames; per-frame first output ≤300 and last output ≤364 cycles |
| Hardware implementation | Default synthesis or imported structural ASAP7 netlist | Complete mapped area; setup/hold at 10 ns |
| RTL/mapped comparison | Representative numerical, protocol and reset cases | Same output data, valid/start signals and clock cycles |
| Throughput search | All 321 integer intervals, II=64–384; at least 1,024 RTL frames each | Shortest passing II, followed by a mapped confirmation subset of 128 frames plus gap/reset probes |
| STA period certification | Reconstraint of one fixed mapped netlist | Setup/hold-passing endpoint with ≤0.01 ns bracket, unless the configured scan floor is reached |

For numerical feasibility, use the **minimum SQNR over nonzero tested frames**, not the average. For latency, use the **maximum observed first-output and completion delays across frames**, not the first transaction. The throughput metric uses the smallest empirically verified II, not an Agent-declared value. Failure at an optional shorter II does not invalidate mandatory 384-cycle operation.

## 2. Public evaluation

From the repository root:

```bash
bash fft64_benchmark/setup.sh --check-only
bash fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh submission runs/quick --quick --no-build
bash fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh submission runs/full --no-build
```

Use `--backend commercial` or `--backend local` to select explicitly. Automatic preparation prefers available commercial tools; otherwise the open-source fallback uses Icarus/Verilator, Yosys/ABC, and OpenSTA. This is **pre-layout** mapping and timing, not complete OpenROAD place-and-route. The selected backend is fixed during a run; tool or license failures do not trigger an undocumented switch. Complete public evaluations return valid component and combined preview scores using the published numeric scales, without private calibration. Final hidden grading also requires matching private platform/protocol validation.

The full architecture profile performs a long-stream test at every integer II. It batches at most eight intervals at a time and preallocates regular input schedules; all 321 intervals and 1,024 frames per interval are retained. Each completed chunk records array sizes, runtime and Python-process peak RSS; EDA subprocess memory requires separate measurement. Use quick numerical/protocol tests to reject unsuitable candidates before running ASIC and capacity evaluation. A quick PASS is **not** full hardware feasibility.

## 3. Agent-controlled synthesis

To create editable optimization scripts:

```bash
bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow
```

After editing `submission/flow/`, build and export `submission/implementation/mapped.v` and its manifest using [OPTIMIZATION.md](../OPTIMIZATION.md). An exported mapped netlist is imported for independent measurement. The evaluator does not run submitted Tcl, Yosys or ABC scripts in private scoring; it checks mapped-cell legality, source/manifest consistency, timing, and representative RTL/netlist behavior. With no custom export, the frozen default mapping is used. If custom recipes exist without a complete export, full evaluation requires the Agent to build first; quick checks remain RTL-only.

## 4. What the evidence supports

Long-stream capacity is a measured result over **finite frames and the tested II range**; it is not proof of a globally minimal II. Large RTL datasets and smaller mapped-netlist subsets establish different coverage. The tool flow gives **pre-layout**, ideal-interconnect standard-cell area and STA estimates, not post-route frequency, power or silicon performance. Optional formal equivalence is reported separately.

Record the backend, tool and library identities, submitted RTL, imported netlist hash when present, selected profile, private platform/protocol calibration when grading hidden data, worst SQNR, maximum per-frame latency, verified II and certified period. Do not compare raw results or scores from different backends or profiles.

Completed caches are tied to RTL, imported implementation, recipe manifest, input frames and seeds, simulator/tool versions, technology libraries, evaluation scripts and scoring policy. Changed inputs require a new output directory; corrupt or incomplete records must not become PASS results.

A proven hardware violation is `DESIGN_INVALID` and receives a valid zero score. # FFT64-Quant: Feasibility and Hardware-Quality Scoring

Optimize the combined normalized hardware score, rather than a single PPA metric. The default `architecture` profile uses complete mapped area (60%), verified effective throughput (30%) and worst first-output latency (10%). Every numeric parameter is public in [profiles/policy.json](profiles/policy.json), and a complete public evaluation returns component scores and the combined preview score without private calibration.

## Feasibility and measured quantities

`resolved=true` requires FFT behavior, natural output order, per-frame SQNR >=50 dB, exact zero output for zero input, reset and protocol behavior, sustained II=384 service, first/completion deadlines, 10 ns setup/hold timing and representative RTL/mapped agreement. There is no score threshold or minimum area saving required to pass. Higher SQNR earns no bonus after the constraint is met.

Area A is the complete mapped cell area in um2, including all storage, arithmetic, control and reordering. The measured minimum frame II comes from all integer intervals 64–384, each with at least 1024 continuous RTL frames and representative mapped confirmation at the selected interval. A fixed-netlist STA clock scan supplies passing period P in ns; a claimed II, estimated slack or producer-reported area cannot substitute for these measurements.

\[
T=\frac{10^9}{II_{ver}P}\quad\mathrm{FFTs/s}.
\]

Latency L is the largest first-input to first-output delay over scored frames, in cycles at the common 10 ns clock. Frequency contributes through T only. Completion latency is also a mandatory check.

## Public numerical parameters

| Quantity | Frozen value | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Ideal area A_ideal | 500 um2 | Area component reaches one |
| Half-credit area A_half | 4000 um2 | Area component equals 0.5 |
| Mandatory throughput T_min | 260416.66666666666 FFT/s | 384 cycles at 10 ns |
| Ideal throughput T_ideal | 62500000 FFT/s | II=64 at the 0.25 ns STA scan floor |
| Ideal first-output latency L_ideal | 63 cycles | Last required input arrives at cycle 63 |
| Maximum first-output latency L_max | 300 cycles | Mandatory first-output deadline |
| Architecture weights | 0.60 / 0.30 / 0.10 | Area / throughput / latency |

These are public objective scales, not measurements of one ideal FFT. Achieving score one requires all three ideal values simultaneously. This combination is intentionally demanding; the benchmark does not claim that it is physically achievable. The 4000 um2 area scale provides useful feedback over a broad range of implementations without making a design above an accurate reference area receive zero area credit.

## Continuous score

Let clip(x,0,1) clamp a value to [0,1].

\[
S_A=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{A_{half}-A_{ideal}}{A+A_{half}-2A_{ideal}},0,1\right)
=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{3500}{A+3000},0,1\right).
\]

Area credit decreases continuously for every A>500, remains positive for finite measured area, and equals 0.5 at 4000 um2. There is no zero-credit interval above a reference circuit's area.

\[
S_T=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{\ln(T/T_{min})}{\ln(T_{ideal}/T_{min})},0,1\right)
=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{\ln(T/T_{min})}{\ln(240)},0,1\right).
\]

Each doubling of throughput below the ideal adds the same component gain, ln(2)/ln(240), approximately 0.12647. Throughput remains discriminative up to the maximum supported by the declared II and clock-scan bounds.

\[
S_L=\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{300-L}{300-63},0,1\right),
\qquad S=0.60S_A+0.30S_T+0.10S_L.
\]

The optional `area` profile uses S=S_A and is a separate diagnostic. Use the full `architecture` profile to select the submitted design. Neither recipe names nor a larger number of experiments earns credit.

When comparing candidates, use the weighted changes 0.60 ΔS_A, 0.30 ΔS_T and 0.10 ΔS_L. Raw percentage improvements are not interchangeable under these nonlinear functions. A throughput gain can be outweighed by an area penalty, and a component already at one earns no further credit. Choose the best complete architecture preview rather than the highest area-only diagnostic.

## Public feedback and final hidden grading

A complete public run returns `grade.components`, `grade.weighted_components`, `grade.score`, the measured PPA and public normalization parameters. It sets `score_valid=true`, `scoring_scope=public_preview` and `official_score=false`. This is valid optimization feedback on public data; final acceptance still depends on independent hidden evaluation. Quick checks and unfinished measurements have no complete hardware score.

Final hidden grading uses the identical public formula and numeric scales, with private input data and matching platform/protocol validation calibration. Accurate fixed-point references validate the environment; they do not secretly choose or alter the score denominator. The private seed, reference RTL and execution records remain private. The score alone never establishes that a hidden test was passed.

Commercial and open-source previews report their backend and are not mixed in one ranking. Official DSBench grading uses the declared commercial environment. A tool failure, timeout or missing official validation is unscored infrastructure, while an observed design-specification violation is a valid zero score. Full internal records preserve that distinction.

# FFT64 RTL Interface and Cycle Contract

The submission must include the synthesizable top-level module `fft64_top` with the fixed ports below. A declaration-only template is supplied in `interface/fft64_top.sv`; it is **not** a functional FFT.

```systemverilog
module fft64_top (
    input  wire clk,
    input  wire rst,
    input  wire in_valid,
    input  wire frame_start,
    input  wire signed [15:0] in_re,
    input  wire signed [15:0] in_im,
    output wire out_valid,
    output wire out_start,
    output wire signed [23:0] out_re,
    output wire signed [23:0] out_im
);
    // Design implementation goes here.
endmodule
```

## Input transactions

- Inputs are stable before the rising edge; outputs are observed after that edge, including nonblocking assignment updates.
- A frame begins when `in_valid=1` and `frame_start=1`, then provides **64 consecutive valid complex samples**. The first sample is cycle 0, the last cycle 63.
- The mandatory service interval between frame starts is **at least 384 cycles**, with no input backpressure. Longer and variable gaps are legal, including long intervals beyond a 16-bit counter range.
- Optional throughput tests use 64–383-cycle intervals to find additional *verified* capacity. Failure at an optional faster interval does not invalidate the mandatory service requirement.

## Output transactions and latency

- Each completed frame produces **64 consecutive `out_valid=1` cycles** in natural frequency order.
- Exactly the first output of each frame asserts `out_start=1`; `out_start=0` whenever `out_valid=0`.
- The first output must occur after the last required input, between cycles 63 and 300 inclusive. The last output must occur by cycle 364.
- The grader measures the **maximum per-frame** first-output and completion latency over the tested frames. Latency need not be constant across legal frames.
- Output payload is don't-care outside `out_valid`; inside valid cycles, all output data and control must be known under four-state simulation.

## Reset and hardware restrictions

Synchronous active-high `rst` aborts unfinished frames. An output prefix emitted before a reset need not be retracted, but no unfinished frame may reappear after reset. New frames following reset must be correct. Use only the specified positive-edge `clk`; storage, buffering, ordering logic and control must all be accounted for in the synthesized design. No uncounted SRAM, testbench-dependent lookup, or second clock is allowed.

Input/output real and imaginary fields are two's-complement with **15 fractional bits**. Intermediate representation may change, but the external FFT gain, scale and order may not.
# FFT64 Architecture and Precision Design Guide

This guide identifies possible design directions; it is **not an implementation recipe or optimized solution**. All architectures must compute the same forward, unscaled, natural-order 64-point complex FFT under the specified external protocol.

## FFT computation versus hardware organization

A pure radix-2 decomposition contains six stages of 32 butterfly operations, or 192 butterfly **operations** per transform. The physical implementation need not contain 192 butterfly units: reuse, pipelining and parallelism determine how the computation is mapped to hardware.

| Architecture | Main organization | Potential benefit | Main implementation cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| R2SDF | One streaming path with feedback delays | Regular pipeline | Stage butterflies, storage and control |
| R2²SDF | Paired radix-2 stages with simplified rotations | Fewer nontrivial twiddle rotations | Feedback alignment and coefficient handling |
| R4MDC | Multiple parallel paths and commutators | Higher intrinsic parallel throughput | Arithmetic duplication, data movement and serial interface adaptation |
| Folded/iterative | Shared butterfly units with scheduled storage accesses | Reduced arithmetic duplication | Memory banking/ports, scheduling and latency |
| Fully parallel | Many simultaneous operations | Short computation latency with sufficient interface bandwidth | High complete-design area and routing overhead |

The 384-cycle minimum service requirement and one-complex-sample-per-cycle interface apply to **every** candidate. A design with more internal parallelism may or may not achieve a better verified throughput after accounting for input/output adaptation.

## Numerical precision choices

Candidate variables include intermediate data widths, guard bits, twiddle-factor widths, truncation or round-to-nearest-even, fixed-point scaling and quantization locations. Trivial rotations (such as multiplication by ±1 or ±j) can be specialized exactly. Any precision reduction must be evaluated on the **complete 64-point output**, using the float64 FFT of the same already-quantized input. Minimum per-frame SQNR—not local butterfly error or average SQNR—determines numerical feasibility.

Keep intentional **fixed-point quantization** distinct from **exact RTL or Boolean optimizations**. Approximate gate pruning, approximate compressors and arbitrary Boolean-function changes are outside the task.

## EDA optimization choices

The default DC or Yosys/ABC mapping is one possible strategy. Agent-controlled recipes can modify synthesis effort, hierarchy, resource sharing, Boolean rewriting and technology mapping. Use the public [optimization interface](../OPTIMIZATION.md) to export a structural netlist; private evaluation independently imports and measures it. A smaller logic count in an intermediate representation does not necessarily imply a smaller or faster complete mapped FFT.

## Useful experimental questions

- Does the memory organization support simultaneous accesses without conflicts?
- Is the natural-order output permutation fully implemented and counted?
- Does a shorter internal processing schedule pass long continuous-frame tests?
- Does lower precision remain feasible for low-energy and sign-sensitive inputs?
- Does a synthesis recipe improve final cell area or certified period after independent STA?
- Is a result specific to one backend or stable across repeated runs of the same frozen flow?

Prefer a few well-measured hypotheses to unsupported claims about an architecture's superiority. Physical placement/routing is optional and does not determine the present pre-layout score.

# Agent 可控综合流程：构建、导出与独立评测

本 benchmark 允许 Agent 同时探索 **RTL 架构与精度**和 **EDA 综合优化策略**。系统提供默认脚本，Agent 可在独立的公开开发环境中替换优化命令、参数和执行顺序。**正式评测不会执行所提交的任意 Tcl、Yosys 或 ABC 脚本；它评估 Agent 已导出的完整标准单元网表。**

## 1. 初始化可编辑模板

在 `FFT-Bench/` 根目录运行：

```bash
bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow
```

命令仅创建缺失文件，不覆盖已有修改，也不要求本机安装 EDA 工具。

| 文件 | 执行阶段 | 可探索的选择 |
|---|---|---|
| `submission/flow/dc_opt.tcl` | DC 完成 elaboration、link 和初始约束后 | `compile`/`compile_ultra`、effort、flattening、retiming、resource sharing、incremental compile 等 |
| `submission/flow/yosys_opt.ys` | Yosys 已读取 RTL 和 Liberty 后 | `synth`、`opt`、FSM/memory 优化及 pass 顺序 |
| `submission/flow/abc_opt.script` | FF 映射后、组合逻辑技术映射时 | `balance`、`rewrite`、`refactor`、`resyn2` 风格序列和映射策略 |
| `submission/flow/pnr_opt.tcl` | 可选 Innovus 初始化之后 | 布局布线及物理优化；**不参与当前评分** |

`resyn2` 并非可移植的 Yosys 顶层命令；可用 ABC 的一组 `balance`、`rewrite`、`refactor` 等命令构造相应序列。不同 ABC 版本对别名和命令的支持可能不同，请以容器内实际工具为准。ABC 模板最终必须完成合法标准单元映射；`{D}` 在公开构建时被替换为由 `--abc-delay-ps` 指定的目标。

DC 驱动通过 `FFT_AGENT_DC_RECIPE` 加载 Agent 的 Tcl；辅助文件可相对于该脚本所在目录引用。公开构建脚本维护工作目录、时序约束的初始加载、最终层次展开与网表导出。Agent 可以改变综合阶段的优化目标，**不得通过修改最终测量 SDC、Liberty、数值参考或评分公式改变成绩**。

## 2. 在 Synopsys 容器中构建

使用同级 `Synopsys/`（对应容器 `/mnt/mydata`）和 `port.txt`：

```bash
bash synopsys.sh build submission --export --out runs/dc_build
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/dc_check
```

第一条命令在容器内运行 Agent 的优化脚本，并将 `mapped.v`、manifest 及 recipe 副本导出到 `submission/implementation/`。第二条命令在**可信评测流程**中导入并重新测量这些单元。完整 `architecture` profile 还包括长帧 II 测试和频率认证，耗时更长。

也可直接在容器内进行自定义调试：

```bash
bash synopsys.sh exec -- dc_shell -f /mnt/mydata/debug.tcl
```

只在 Agent 自己的工作目录中操作，不要修改全局库、工具配置或其他 Agent 的目录。

## 3. 使用 Yosys/ABC 构建

工具直接安装在本机时：

```bash
bash build_implementation.sh submission --backend local \
  --abc-delay-ps 10000 --out runs/yosys_build --export

bash fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh submission runs/yosys_check \
  --backend local --profile area --no-build
```

也可将 Yosys/ABC 生成的合法 ASAP7 RVT/TT 网表交由 Synopsys 开发评价端测量：

```bash
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/imported_check
```

这种跨工具构建**不会**改变最终的库和测量约束。公开预览在两个后端上都使用已公布的归一化函数与锚点，无需私有校准；同一个导出网表由不同 STA 后端得到的原始 PPA 和分数不得直接混排。正式隐藏评分还需匹配其测量平台和输入协议的校准。

## 4. 导出产物与正式评分边界

自定义综合的交付结构为：

```text
submission/
├── rtl/                  # 产生该实现的完整 RTL
├── flow/                 # 自定义优化 recipe 及辅助文件
└── implementation/
    ├── mapped.v          # 扁平化的结构化 ASAP7 标准单元网表
    ├── manifest.json     # RTL、网表、库和 recipe 的一致性信息
    └── recipes/          # 构建时使用的 recipe 副本
```

评测器检查 manifest 与当前 RTL、网表、固定库哈希的**一致性**，限制导入的结构化内容，独立统计映射单元面积、运行固定约束 STA，并在代表性测试上对比 RTL 与网表。正式隐藏环境不运行 Agent 的优化脚本，也不采用 Agent 自报的面积、频率或 SQNR。

**边界说明：** Agent 可自行编辑或生成 manifest，其哈希验证不构成可信的工具执行证明。因此，结果可信性主要来自评测器对导入网表的独立检查；如果实验要求证明某个 recipe 确实生成了网表，应另由可信构建环境保存带工具身份的执行记录。

对 RTL 或 recipe 作出更改后，应重新导出网表，使用新的构建与评测输出目录；不要将不同候选的报告或缓存混用。没有自定义 recipe 和网表时，正式评测采用冻结的默认综合流程。只有提交 recipe 而没有完整导出实现时，完整评价会拒绝继续，`--quick` 仍可进行 RTL-only 开发检查。

## 5. 评价范围与公平性

- **强制可行性：** FFT、逐帧 SQNR、输入/输出协议、复位、384-cycle 服务、10 ns 时序、RTL/网表一致性。
- **硬件质量：** 完整映射面积、经长时间验证的 II、STA 认证周期和最大首输出延迟。
- **固定测量条件：** ASAP7 RVT/TT、数值参考、正式 SDC、结果统计和评分标尺。
- **允许的优化：** 精确布尔重写、常数特化、资源共享、合法流水与复用，以及显式定点量化。
- **禁止的优化：** 任意门级 ALS/逻辑破坏、依赖测试数据的作弊实现、修改评分或隐藏检查。

准确参考设计使用冻结的默认映射 recipe 验证平台和协议，**其面积、吞吐率和延迟不设定归一化锚点**。候选可以使用其他 recipe，额外收益可以进入同一后端的硬件质量评分。完整公开 `architecture` 评测返回分项及总分，供 Agent 比较 RTL、精度和综合策略；`area` profile 仅作诊断。这一设置与仅优化 RTL 的固定 flow 实验不同，分析实验结果时应明确标记。

## 6. 可选物理设计与复现

`pnr_opt.tcl` 只是开发模板。需要匹配的 ASAP7 LEF、RC、site 和供电规划，且物理规模与单位必须经过验证；当前官方指标仍为 **pre-layout synthesis 与 ideal-interconnect STA**，没有 post-route PPA 或功耗分数。

独立输出目录是复现实验的基本要求。构建可在输入身份完全一致时复用产物；远程任务可用 `--resume` 恢复相同快照。工具、RTL、recipe 或库改变后需更换目录；`--export` 会在构建结果内备份被替换的旧实现。

## Objective

Develop a complete, synthesizable **64-point fixed-point complex FFT processor** from the public specification. The task is open-design: no working FFT RTL is supplied. Your objective is to satisfy every mandatory specification and improve the measured hardware quality through architecture selection, precision allocation, RTL optimization and, optionally, synthesis-flow exploration. The evaluated circuit includes its storage, control, data reordering and input/output logic—not only butterfly arithmetic.

## Mandatory contract

- **Transform:** forward, unscaled, 64-point complex FFT; natural-order input and natural-frequency-order output.
- **Data:** 16-bit signed input components and 24-bit signed output components, each with 15 fractional bits. Tested input components lie in [-0.5, 0.5]; nonzero frames have complex RMS ≥1/32.
- **Input service:** one valid complex sample per cycle for 64 consecutive cycles. Frames starting at least 384 cycles apart must be accepted without backpressure.
- **Output:** 64 consecutive valid samples in natural frequency order; `out_start` marks the first output. The first output cannot precede the final required input and must occur by cycle 300, and the last by cycle 364, relative to the first input edge (cycle 0).
- **Reset and clock:** synchronous, active-high reset aborts incomplete work. Only the specified rising-edge clock is allowed; mapped timing must pass the 10 ns requirement.
- **Numerical quality:** every evaluated nonzero frame must achieve SQNR ≥50 dB against the float64 FFT of the **same already-quantized input**. A zero input must produce exactly zero output. No fitted gain, phase, scaling or frequency permutation is permitted.

Here X is the same-input float64 reference and X-hat is the hardware output. SQNR is computed per complete complex frame:
\[
\mathrm{SQNR}_f=10\log_{10}\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{63}|X_f[k]|^2}{\sum_{k=0}^{63}|\hat X_f[k]-X_f[k]|^2}.
\]

The 384-cycle frame interval is the **mandatory minimum service capability**, not a limit on the throughput an architecture may achieve. Faster frame intervals are optional and contribute to the architecture score only when the evaluator verifies them. See [SPEC.json](SPEC.json) and [INTERFACE.md](INTERFACE.md) for the authoritative contract.

## Design freedom and restrictions

Choose a valid FFT architecture, including R2SDF, R2²SDF, R4MDC, folded/iterative designs or other implementations. You may change internal data/twiddle widths, rounding and truncation rules, guard bits, memory organization, pipeline scheduling, exact twiddle specialization and resource sharing. You may also explore synthesis effort, Boolean rewriting, optimization pass ordering and technology mapping.

To use a custom synthesis recipe, initialize `submission/flow/` with `bash build_implementation.sh submission --init-flow`, edit the provided DC or Yosys/ABC templates, and export `submission/implementation/mapped.v` together with `manifest.json`. The evaluator then **imports and measures the mapped standard-cell netlist**, checks it against the submitted RTL and enforces its own technology library, STA and numerical requirements. **Private scoring never executes submitted optimization scripts** or trusts self-reported PPA. For commands and build requirements, read [OPTIMIZATION.md](../OPTIMIZATION.md).

Approximate gate pruning, arbitrary approximate Boolean transformations, unrelated approximate compressors, simulation-only lookup implementations and modifications to the external FFT/streaming contract are forbidden. Explicit fixed-point quantization is permitted, but SQNR must remain feasible. Uncounted external SRAM or logic is not allowed. Optional P&R recipes are for development and do not affect the current pre-layout score.

## Recommended execution

1. Read [SPEC.json](SPEC.json), [INTERFACE.md](INTERFACE.md), [ARCHITECTURE_GUIDE.md](ARCHITECTURE_GUIDE.md), [SCORING.md](SCORING.md) and [EVALUATION.md](EVALUATION.md).
2. Create `submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md` with at least two architecture hypotheses and measurable expected trade-offs.
3. Implement a correct baseline in `submission/rtl/` and run public numerical/protocol checks.
4. Explore promising RTL, quantization and synthesis-recipe changes; measure complete mapped area and timing on the same backend.
5. Use long multi-frame capacity tests for promising candidates. Record measured results, failures and revised design decisions in `measurements.csv`.
6. Submit the best **verified** implementation, including a rebuilt mapped export if custom synthesis was used.

With a sibling `Synopsys/` mount and `port.txt`, run from the **FFT-Bench repository root**:

```bash
bash check_env.sh
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --quick --out runs/quick
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile area --out runs/area
bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/full
```

You may invoke the container's tools directly using `bash synopsys.sh exec -- <command>`. See [REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md](../REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md). If tools are installed locally, use `fft64_benchmark/run_preview.sh`. Use separate run directories for different RTL or recipes; a quick PASS is not full ASIC feasibility.

## Evaluation and deliverables

`resolved=true` requires numerical correctness, streaming/reset behavior, mandatory II=384 service, first/completion latency, mapped-netlist checks and 10 ns setup/hold timing. There is **no minimum area-reduction threshold**. Optimize the combined normalized `architecture` score: 0.60 S_A + 0.30 S_T + 0.10 S_L. Its public scales are area ideal/half-credit 500/4000 um2, throughput minimum/ideal 260416.66666666666/62500000 FFT/s, and latency ideal/maximum 63/300 cycles. Read SCORING.md for the exact rational-area, logarithmic-throughput and linear-latency functions. SQNR above 50 dB does not earn a bonus. Numerical feasibility uses the minimum frame-level SQNR, latency uses the maximum observed per-frame value, and throughput uses the smallest **tested and verified** integer II in 64–384—not a value declared by the Agent.

The ideal anchors form an intentionally demanding scoring scale, not a claim that one physical circuit achieves all three. Area credit stays positive above the half-credit anchor; throughput credit is logarithmic; each component saturates at one. Compare weighted component changes (0.60 ΔS_A, 0.30 ΔS_T, 0.10 ΔS_L), and select the highest verified combined score. Use the area profile to screen candidates, not to choose the final architecture winner.

The public evaluation uses at least 1,024 random nonzero frames; private hidden evaluation uses at least 8,192, both supplemented by directed inputs. Each candidate II is tested with at least 1,024 consecutive RTL frames, followed by representative mapped confirmation at the selected shortest passing II. These are empirical checks, not formal guarantees. All normalization functions and numeric targets are public. Complete public evaluation returns measured component scores and a combined preview score without private calibration. Final hidden grading additionally requires matching platform/protocol validation. Do not compare different backends or profiles.

Submit:

- `submission/rtl/`: self-contained synthesizable RTL with top module `fft64_top`;
- `submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md`: short hypothesis/experiment/decision record;
- `submission/measurements.csv`: actual measurements of significant candidates;
- `submission/design_config.json` (optional): RTL source list and non-authoritative II hint;
- `submission/flow/` and `submission/implementation/` when using custom synthesis: optimization recipe, complete mapped netlist and manifest.

The grader determines results independently. Do not alter the specification, scoring scripts, hidden data or calibration; do not fabricate measurements or change the submission after private feedback.
# Evidence-Driven Design Workflow

The evaluation rewards the final verified FFT implementation, not the length of a design journal. Maintain a short decision record so that architecture, precision and tool-flow choices can be explained by **actual measurements**.

## Recommended process

1. **Read the contract.** Inspect `TASK_EN.md` or `TASK_ZH.md`, `SPEC.json` and `INTERFACE.md`. Read SCORING.md and every numeric target in profiles/policy.json before choosing an architecture. Optimize 0.60 S_A + 0.30 S_T + 0.10 S_L; separate mandatory II=384 service from optional higher throughput.
2. **Form competing hypotheses.** Consider at least two FFT architectures with different area, storage, scheduling and throughput characteristics. The [architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE_GUIDE.md) provides options without prescribing a solution.
3. **Create a working baseline.** Implement synthesizable RTL and pass public functional, protocol and SQNR tests before optimizing area or II.
4. **Change one meaningful design choice.** Explore a hardware structure, explicit fixed-point quantization rule, or [EDA synthesis recipe](../OPTIMIZATION.md). State the expected effect and the measurement that could disprove it.
5. **Measure and compare.** Start with quick checks; synthesize and evaluate promising candidates with the same backend and reference policy. Use grade.components, grade.weighted_components and grade.score from complete architecture previews to compare trade-offs. Preserve negative experiments when they inform a decision.
6. **Revise the plan.** Update `DESIGN_PLAN.md` after material changes and append measured configurations to `measurements.csv`. Distinguish estimates from EDA measurements and partial tests from full scores.
7. **Freeze the best verified candidate.** Keep RTL, source and recipe hashes, and—when using custom synthesis—the exported structural netlist and manifest. Rebuild after changing RTL or recipe. Do not use private feedback to revise a submitted candidate.

With sibling `Synopsys/` and `port.txt`, use `check_env.sh`, `run_synopsys_debug.sh` and `synopsys.sh exec` for publicly authorized container debugging. Work in a separate output directory for each design candidate. See [REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md](../REMOTE_SYNOPSYS.md).

## Suggested measurement schema

```text
id,architecture,precision_policy,source_hash,recipe_hash,mapped_hash,backend,library_id,area_um2,worst_sqnr_db,verified_ii_cycles,certified_period_ns,maximum_first_cycles,maximum_completion_cycles,area_score,throughput_score,latency_score,total_score,score_valid,scoring_scope,timing_pass,protocol_pass,status,notes
```

Leave unavailable values blank rather than using zero. Record component scores and total score only when the selected profile's complete evaluation returns valid feedback. Compare 0.60 ΔS_A, 0.30 ΔS_T and 0.10 ΔS_L when selecting the final design; a saturated component earns no further credit, and an area-only score cannot substitute for the combined objective. The `frame_ii_cycles` configuration field is a hint; official throughput is independently measured. A custom implementation's area and timing must be evaluated using the same frozen library and constraints as competing designs. """Continuous-frame verification and empirical minimum-II qualification."""

def validate_interval(interval):
    settings=profile_policy('architecture')['claimed_ii']
    if(type(interval)is not int or not settings['minimum']<=interval<=settings['maximum']):
        raise ValueError('frame_ii_cycles must be an integer from 64 through 384')
    return interval


def stream_schedule(frames,interval,seed=11,tail=True,reset_probes=True):
    validate_interval(interval)
    frames=np.asarray(frames,dtype=np.int64);rng=np.random.default_rng(seed)
    if not tail and not reset_probes and len(frames):
        # The exhaustive scan needs a regular stream. Allocate it directly:
        # avoid a large temporary Python list of per-cycle rows.
        starts=5+np.arange(len(frames),dtype=np.int64)*interval
        events=np.zeros((int(starts[-1])+64+400,5),dtype=np.int64)
        events[:3,0]=1
        for start,frame in zip(starts,frames):
            events[start:start+64,1]=1;events[start,2]=1
            events[start:start+64,3:5]=frame
        metadata=dict(frame_starts=starts.tolist(),offered_min_frame_II=interval,clock_period_ns=10,
            ignore_before_cycle=5,cancelled_partial_start=None,reset_probes=[],
            continuous_frames=len(frames),mixed_gap_tail_frames=0,
            offered_frame_intervals=[interval]if len(frames)>1 else[])
        return events,metadata,frames
    ev=[[1,0,0,0,0]]*3+[[0,0,0,0,0]]*2;probes=[]
    if reset_probes:
        for count,partial in [(8,False),(4,True)]:
            begin=len(ev)
            for j in range(count):
                x=frames[j%len(frames)]
                ev.extend([0,1,int(k==0),int(z[0]),int(z[1])]for k,z in enumerate(x))
                ev.extend([[0,0,0,0,0]]*(interval-64))
            if partial:
                ev.extend([0,1,int(k==0),int(z[0]),int(z[1])]for k,z in enumerate(frames[0][:20]))
            else:ev.extend([[0,0,0,0,0]]*17)
            probes.append(dict(epoch_start=begin,full_frames_offered=count,partial_frame=partial,reset_cycle=len(ev)))
            ev.extend([[1,0,0,0,0]]*3+[[0,0,0,0,0]]*3)
    ignore=len(ev);starts=[]
    extra_indices=rng.integers(0,len(frames),size=16)if tail else[]
    allframes=np.concatenate([frames,frames[extra_indices]],axis=0)if tail else frames
    for j,x in enumerate(allframes):
        starts.append(len(ev))
        ev.extend([0,1,int(k==0),int(z[0]),int(z[1])]for k,z in enumerate(x))
        if j<len(frames)-1:gap=interval-64
        elif j==len(frames)-1 and tail:gap=65568+384
        elif tail:gap=[interval,interval+1,interval+7,384][(j-len(frames))%4]-64
        else:gap=0
        ev.extend([[0,0,0,0,0]]*gap)
    ev.extend([[0,0,0,0,0]]*400)
    metadata=dict(frame_starts=starts,offered_min_frame_II=interval,clock_period_ns=10,
                  ignore_before_cycle=ignore,cancelled_partial_start=probes[-1]['epoch_start']if probes else None,
                  reset_probes=probes,continuous_frames=len(frames),mixed_gap_tail_frames=len(extra_indices),
                  offered_frame_intervals=sorted(set(np.diff(starts).tolist())))
    return np.asarray(ev,dtype=np.int64),metadata,allframes


def probe_intervals(source,frames,outdir,backend='vcs',seed=11):
    """Every tested II receives >=1024 consecutive frames; no short pilot."""
    out=Path(outdir);out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    settings=profile_policy('architecture')['ii_calibration']
    identity=dict(backend=backend,source_sha256=hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(),
                  frames=array_identity(frames),seed=seed,runtime=runtime_identity(backend),settings=settings)
    with lock(out/'lock'):
        bind_directory(out,identity)
        return _probe_intervals(source,frames,out,backend,seed,identity)


def _probe_intervals(source,frames,out,backend,seed,identity):
    started=time.monotonic()
    checkpoint=out/'probe_results.json'
    settings=profile_policy('architecture')['ii_calibration'];count=settings['pilot_frames_per_interval']
    if len(frames)<count:raise ValueError('Throughput trial needs at least 1024 frames')
    lo,hi=settings['pilot_all_integer_intervals']
    def valid(rows,begin,end):
        return (isinstance(rows,list) and len(rows)==end-begin and
            all(isinstance(row,dict) and row.get('frame_ii_cycles')==interval and
                row.get('tested_frames')==count and type(row.get('pass_rtl'))is bool and
                (not row['pass_rtl'] or isinstance(row.get('quality'),dict))
                for interval,row in zip(range(begin,end),rows)))
    cached=load_cached(checkpoint,identity)
    if valid(cached,lo,hi+1):return cached
    rng=np.random.default_rng(seed);indices=rng.choice(len(frames),size=count,replace=False)
    selected=np.asarray(frames)[indices];results=[];compiled=None;maximum_batch_input_bytes=0
    chunk_size=settings['chunk_intervals'];(out/'latencies').mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    save(out/'probe_protocol.json',dict(intervals=[lo,hi],frame_indices=indices.tolist(),frames_per_interval=count,
        fft_length=64,method='exhaustive integer-II long RTL measurements; no claimed-II score'))
    for begin in range(lo,hi+1,chunk_size):
        chunk_started=time.monotonic()
        end=min(hi+1,begin+chunk_size);chunk=out/('intervals_'+str(begin)+'_'+str(end-1));chunk.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        saved=chunk/'results.json'
        chunk_identity=dict(identity,intervals=[begin,end-1])
        cached=load_cached(saved,chunk_identity)
        if valid(cached,begin,end):
            results.extend(cached)
            if compiled is None and(chunk/'simulation/simv').exists():compiled=chunk/'simulation'
            continue
        events=[];epochs=[];offset=0
        for interval in range(begin,end):
            e,m,_=stream_schedule(selected,interval,seed,tail=False,reset_probes=False)
            events.append(e);epochs.append((interval,offset,len(e),m));offset+=len(e)
        batch=np.concatenate(events,axis=0);del events
        maximum_batch_input_bytes=max(maximum_batch_input_bytes,batch.nbytes)
        raw=simulate(source,batch,chunk/'simulation',backend,probe=True,reuse_compiled_from=compiled)
        if compiled is None:compiled=chunk/'simulation'
        measured=[]
        for interval,start,length,metadata in epochs:
            item=dict(frame_ii_cycles=interval,tested_frames=count,pass_rtl=False)
            e=batch[start:start+length];r=raw[start:start+length].copy();r[:,0]-=start
            try:
                outputs,lat=decode(r,e,metadata);q=quality(selected,outputs)
                item.update(pass_rtl=bool(q['feasible']),minimum_sqnr_db=q['minimum_frame_sqnr_db'],quality=q,
                            maximum_first_output_cycles=lat['maximum_first_output_latency_cycles'],
                            maximum_completion_cycles=lat['maximum_frame_completion_cycles'])
                np.savez_compressed(out/'latencies'/('ii_'+str(interval)+'.npz'),
                    first=lat['per_frame_first_output_latency_cycles'],completion=lat['per_frame_completion_cycles'])
                if not q['feasible']:item['reason']='SQNR or exact-zero failure'
            except (AssertionError,ValueError)as exc:item['reason']=str(exc)[:400]
            measured.append(item)
        save_cached(saved,measured,chunk_identity);results.extend(measured)
        save(chunk/'resources.json',dict(intervals=[begin,end-1],cycles=len(batch),
            input_array_bytes=batch.nbytes,output_array_bytes=raw.nbytes,
            wall_seconds=time.monotonic()-chunk_started,
            python_process_peak_rss_kib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
            scope='Python process lifetime peak; excludes EDA subprocess memory'))
        save(out/'progress.json',dict(status='RUNNING',completed_intervals=len(results),total_intervals=hi-lo+1,
            frames_per_interval=count,last_interval=end-1,chunk_intervals=chunk_size,
            maximum_batch_input_bytes=maximum_batch_input_bytes,
            process_peak_rss_kib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss))
        del raw,batch
    with(out/'intervals.csv').open('w',newline='')as stream:
        writer=csv.DictWriter(stream,['frame_ii_cycles','tested_frames','pass_rtl','minimum_sqnr_db','maximum_first_output_cycles','maximum_completion_cycles','reason'],extrasaction='ignore')
        writer.writeheader();writer.writerows(results)
    save(out/'progress.json',dict(status='COMPLETE',completed_intervals=len(results),frames_per_interval=count,
        wall_seconds=time.monotonic()-started,process_peak_rss_kib=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
        chunk_intervals=chunk_size,maximum_batch_input_bytes=maximum_batch_input_bytes,
        resource_scope='current Python process; tool subprocess resources are recorded separately'))
    save_cached(checkpoint,results,identity)

def qualify(source,mapped_source,frames,outdir,interval,backend='vcs',seed=11,
            rtl_compiled=None,gate_compiled=None):
    interval=validate_interval(interval);out=Path(outdir)/('ii_'+str(interval));out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    identity=dict(backend=backend,source_sha256=hashlib.sha256(source.encode()).hexdigest(),
                  mapped_source_sha256=hashlib.sha256(mapped_source.encode()).hexdigest(),
                  frames=array_identity(frames),interval=interval,seed=seed,runtime=runtime_identity(backend),
                  mapped_runtime=runtime_identity('verilator'if backend=='iverilog'else backend),
                  gate_initial_state_modes=[0,1,20261121]if backend=='vcs'else[None])
    with lock(out/'lock'):
        bind_directory(out,identity)
        return _qualify(source,mapped_source,frames,out,interval,backend,seed,rtl_compiled,gate_compiled,identity)


def _qualify(source,mapped_source,frames,out,interval,backend,seed,rtl_compiled,gate_compiled,identity):
    path=out/'qualification.json'

    if isinstance(cached,dict) and cached.get('status')in{'PASS','FAIL'}:return cached

"""Public optimization worker: editable native recipes, structural artifact export."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import time
from common import ROOT,TECH,COMB,SEQ,run,save,sha,read,lock,CacheIdentityError
from toolchain import activate,find_tool,prepare
from implementation import validate_structural,export_artifacts


def initialize(submission):
    directory=Path(submission)/'flow';directory.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    for name in ['dc_opt.tcl','yosys_opt.ys','abc_opt.script','pnr_opt.tcl']:
        target=directory/name
        if not target.exists():shutil.copy2(ROOT/'flow/templates'/name,target)
    return directory


def q(path):
    return '"'+str(path).replace('\\','\\\\').replace('"','\\"')+'"'


def build(submission,outdir,backend='commercial',abc_delay_ps=10000,timeout=1800):
    from evaluate import assemble
    activate();submission=Path(submission).resolve();out=Path(outdir).resolve();out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    source,info=assemble(submission,include_implementation=False)
    names=['dc_opt.tcl']if backend=='commercial'else['yosys_opt.ys','abc_opt.script']
    tools=['dc_shell']if backend=='commercial'else['yosys','abc']
    selected={name:find_tool(name)for name in tools}
    if not all(selected.values()):raise EnvironmentError('Required build tools missing: '+str(selected))
    recipes={name:(submission/'flow'/name if (submission/'flow'/name).is_file()else ROOT/'flow/templates'/name)for name in names}
    custom={str(p.relative_to(submission/'flow')):sha(p)for p in sorted((submission/'flow').rglob('*'))if p.is_file()}if(submission/'flow').is_dir()else{}
    identity=dict(rtl_sha256=info['source_sha256'],backend=backend,abc_delay_ps=abc_delay_ps,
        recipes={name:sha(path)for name,path in recipes.items()},custom_files=custom,
        libraries={p.name:sha(p)for p in [COMB,SEQ]},
        tools={name:dict(path=path,sha256=sha(path))for name,path in selected.items()},
        worker_sha256=sha(__file__),dc_driver_sha256=sha(ROOT/'flow/build_dc.tcl'))
    with lock(out/'build.lock'):
        signature=out/'build_identity.json'
        if signature.exists()and read(signature)!=identity:raise CacheIdentityError('Build inputs changed; choose a new build output directory')
        save(signature,identity)
        artifact=out/'implementation';manifest=artifact/'manifest.json'
        if manifest.exists()and(artifact/'mapped.v').exists():
            cached=read(manifest)
            if cached.get('mapped_sha256')==sha(artifact/'mapped.v'):
                return dict(status='BUILT',reused=True,implementation=str(artifact),manifest=cached)
        started=time.monotonic();work=out/'build';work.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (work/'source.sv').write_text(source)
        recipe_dir=work/'flow'
        if(submission/'flow').is_dir():shutil.copytree(submission/'flow',recipe_dir,dirs_exist_ok=True)
        recipe_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        for name,path in recipes.items():shutil.copy2(path,recipe_dir/name)
        old={key:os.environ.get(key)for key in ['FFT_WORK','FFT_TASK_ROOT','FFT_TECH_DIR','FFT_AGENT_DC_RECIPE','FFT_MAPPED_OUTPUT']}
        os.environ.update(FFT_WORK=str(work),FFT_TASK_ROOT=str(ROOT),FFT_TECH_DIR=str(TECH),
            FFT_AGENT_DC_RECIPE=str(recipe_dir/'dc_opt.tcl'),FFT_MAPPED_OUTPUT=str(work/'mapped.v'))
        try:
            if backend=='commercial':
                run(['dc_shell','-f',ROOT/'flow/build_dc.tcl'],work/'dc_build.log',timeout,cwd=work)
                from commercial import check_log
                check_log(work/'dc_build.log')
            else:
                abc_text='\n'.join(line for line in (recipe_dir/'abc_opt.script').read_text().splitlines()if not line.lstrip().startswith('#'))+'\n'
                abc_text=abc_text.replace('{D}','-D '+format(abc_delay_ps,'g'))
                (work/'abc_opt.script').write_text(abc_text)
                (work/'abc.constr').write_text('set_driving_cell BUFx2_ASAP7_75t_R\nset_load 1\n')
                ys=f'read_liberty -lib {q(COMB)}\nread_liberty -lib {q(SEQ)}\nread_verilog -sv {q(work/"source.sv")}\n'
                ys+=(recipe_dir/'yosys_opt.ys').read_text()+'\n'
                ys+=f'dfflibmap -liberty {q(SEQ)}\nabc -exe {q(selected["abc"])} -liberty {q(COMB)} -constr abc.constr -D {abc_delay_ps} -script abc_opt.script\n'
                ys+=f'flatten\nclean\ncheck\nwrite_verilog -noattr -noexpr {q(work/"mapped.v")}\nstat\n'
                (work/'build.ys').write_text(ys)
                run(['yosys','-Q','-T','-s',work/'build.ys'],work/'yosys_build.log',timeout,cwd=work)
            mapped=validate_structural((work/'mapped.v').read_text())
            artifact.mkdir(exist_ok=True);(artifact/'mapped.v').write_text(mapped)
            provenance=dict(rtl_sha256=info['source_sha256'],mapped_sha256=sha(artifact/'mapped.v'),
                libraries_sha256={p.name:sha(p)for p in [COMB,SEQ]},
                producer=dict(backend=backend,tools=identity['tools'],recipe_sha256=identity['recipes'],
                              custom_files_sha256=custom,abc_delay_ps=abc_delay_ps),
                build_seconds=time.monotonic()-started,
                evaluation='Area/timing are measured independently; producer reports are not scores')
            shutil.copytree(recipe_dir,artifact/'recipes',dirs_exist_ok=True)
            save(manifest,provenance)
            result=dict(status='BUILT',reused=False,implementation=str(artifact),manifest=provenance)
            save(out/'build_result.json',result);return result
        finally:
            for key,value in old.items():
                if value is None:os.environ.pop(key,None)
                else:os.environ[key]=value


def main(argv=None):
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('submission');parser.add_argument('--out')
    parser.add_argument('--backend',choices=['local','commercial'],default='local')
    parser.add_argument('--init-flow',action='store_true');parser.add_argument('--export',action='store_true')
    parser.add_argument('--abc-delay-ps',type=float,default=10000)
    parser.add_argument('--timeout',type=int,default=1800)
    args=parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.abc_delay_ps<=0 or args.timeout<=0:parser.error('Delay target and timeout must be positive')
    if args.init_flow:
        print(initialize(args.submission));return 0
    if not args.out:parser.error('--out is required')
    if args.backend=='commercial':
        environment=prepare('commercial',allow_build=False)
        if not environment['ready']:raise EnvironmentError('Commercial build environment is not ready: '+str(environment))
    result=build(args.submission,args.out,args.backend,args.abc_delay_ps,args.timeout)
    if args.export:result['exported_to']=str(export_artifacts(result['implementation'],args.submission,Path(args.out)/'export_backup'))
    print(json.dumps(result,indent=2));return 0


if __name__=='__main__':sys.exit(main())
"}

"""Clock-scan certification on one fixed mapped ASIC netlist."""
from pathlib import Path
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import shutil
from common import ROOT,run,save,read,sha,lock
from scoring import profile_policy,POLICY_SHA256
from toolchain import find_tool


def validate_trials(endpoint,trials,settings):
    if endpoint.get('status')!='CERTIFIED' or not endpoint.get('hold_pass'):
        raise EnvironmentError('No passing setup/hold frequency endpoint')
    passing=endpoint['passing_period_ns'];failing=endpoint.get('failing_period_ns')
    for row in trials:
        for key in ['period_ns','actual_clock_period_ns','setup_slack_ns','hold_slack_ns']:
            if not math.isfinite(row[key]):raise EnvironmentError('Nonfinite STA scan measurement')
        if abs(row['period_ns']-row['actual_clock_period_ns'])>1e-6:
            raise EnvironmentError('STA scan did not apply the requested clock')
    point=[r for r in trials if abs(r['period_ns']-passing)<1e-8 and r['pass']]
    if not point or min(point[-1]['setup_slack_ns'],point[-1]['hold_slack_ns'])<0:
        raise EnvironmentError('Passing clock was not measured successfully')
    if endpoint.get('capped_at_minimum_period'):
        if failing is not None or abs(passing-settings['minimum_period_ns'])>1e-8:
            raise EnvironmentError('Invalid scan-cap endpoint')
    else:
        if(failing is None or failing>=passing
           or passing-failing>settings['resolution_ns']+1e-9):
            raise EnvironmentError('Invalid passing/failing frequency bracket')
        bad=[r for r in trials if abs(r['period_ns']-failing)<1e-8 and r['setup_slack_ns']<0]
        if not bad:raise EnvironmentError('Failing endpoint has no measured setup violation')
    if len(trials)!=endpoint.get('trials'):raise EnvironmentError('Incomplete frequency scan trace')


def certify(asic,backend='commercial'):
    if backend=='local':
        from local_frequency import certify_local
        return certify_local(asic)
    from commercial import check_log
    asic=Path(asic).resolve()
    settings=profile_policy('architecture')['fmax_scan']
    pt=find_tool('pt_shell')
    if not pt:raise EnvironmentError('PrimeTime is required for official frequency certification')
    identity=dict(mapped_sha256=sha(asic/'mapped.v'),script_sha256=sha(ROOT/'flow/fmax_pt.tcl'),
                  pt_path=pt,pt_sha256=sha(pt),scan=settings,policy_sha256=POLICY_SHA256,
                  mapping_signature=read(asic/'signature.json'))
    key=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(identity,sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:24]
    work=asic/'frequency_certificates'/key
    with lock(work/'lock'):
        if(work/'certificate.json').exists():return read(work/'certificate.json'),work
        shutil.copy2(asic/'mapped.v',work/'mapped.v')
        save(work/'identity.json',identity)
        keys=['FFT_WORK','FFT_TASK_ROOT','FFT_FMAX_MIN_PS','FFT_FMAX_MAX_PS','FFT_FMAX_TOL_PS','FFT_FMAX_ITERATIONS']
        previous={k:os.environ.get(k)for k in keys}
        os.environ.update(FFT_WORK=str(work),FFT_TASK_ROOT=str(ROOT),
                          FFT_FMAX_MIN_PS=str(settings['minimum_period_ns']*1000),
                          FFT_FMAX_MAX_PS=str(settings['maximum_period_ns']*1000),
                          FFT_FMAX_TOL_PS=str(settings['resolution_ns']*1000),
                          FFT_FMAX_ITERATIONS=str(settings['maximum_iterations']))
        try:
            run(['pt_shell','-f',ROOT/'flow/fmax_pt.tcl'],work/'fmax.log',600,cwd=work)
            check_log(work/'fmax.log')
            endpoint=read(work/'fmax_scan/endpoint.json')
            with(work/'fmax_scan/trials.csv').open(newline='')as stream:
                trials=[dict(trial=int(r['trial']),period_ns=float(r['period_ns']),
                             actual_clock_period_ns=float(r['actual_clock_period_ns']),
                             setup_slack_ns=float(r['setup_slack_ns']),hold_slack_ns=float(r['hold_slack_ns']),
                             **{'pass':r['pass']=='1'})for r in csv.DictReader(stream)]
            validate_trials(endpoint,trials,settings)
            check=(work/'fmax_scan/check_at_passing.rpt').read_text()
            if __import__('re').search(r'(?im)^\s*Warning:.*(?:unconstrained|no[_ ]clock|no[_ ]input[_ ]delay|no[_ ]output[_ ]delay)',check):
                raise EnvironmentError('Frequency scan has unconstrained paths')
            certificate=dict(endpoint,**identity,trial_trace_sha256=sha(work/'fmax_scan/trials.csv'),
                             certified_frequency_MHz=1000/endpoint['passing_period_ns'],
                             measurement='PrimeTime setup/hold passing endpoint on a fixed mapped netlist; pre-layout',
                             certificate_directory=str(work))
            save(work/'certificate.json',certificate)
            return certificate,work
        finally:
            for k,v in previous.items():
                if v is None:os.environ.pop(k,None)
                else:os.environ[k]=v

products for each remaining complex multiplication; same numerical result,

area/throughput gains exceed the0.00084388 latency-score cost.

benchmark constraints; producer timing is not frequency certification.

clock-target steering still demonstrably changes mapping and timing.
Full frequency scans, gate comparisons and II searches remain pending for
candidates not yet marked COMPLETE in measurements.csv.

## Data-path organization

Each paired DIF group forms a=x0+x2, b=x1+x3, c=x0-x2, d=x1-x3.
The first SDF stage applies only the exact -j rotation to d. The second
forms (a+b), (a-b), (c-j*d), (c+j*d) in four successive quarters, then
applies twiddle powers0,2*j,j,3*j respectively. The next pair uses the same
identity on16-point groups; the final4-point groups require no nontrivial
coefficient. This implements the full forward FFT without frame scaling.

Pipeline data memories need no reset. A reset clears all valid/start delay
chains, frame counters and reorder controls. Every selected valid datum has
been overwritten by the new complete frame before use. Reset aborts an
inflight output prefix by dropping valid. All registers use the given
positive-edge clock; the synthesized flop arrays and all muxes are counted.

The staged-precision candidates accept Q15 external input, use RNE when
converting to Q14, and maintain one guard bit per butterfly. After paired
stages2 and4, RNE reduces Q14->Q13 and Q13->Q12. Final19-bit Q12 samples are
sign-extended and shifted left3 into the external24-bit Q15 fields; this
restores the fixed-point representation, without changing FFT gain. Both
remaining complex rotations use signed Q9 coefficients and one rounding
boundary after exact products/sums. C004 adds registers before and after
three-real-product arithmetic and predecodes coefficients before their
registers. C005 tests a shared one-hot decoder/OR reduction for the64-word

''')

# FFT64-Quant: design and measured selection

## Objective and constraints
Architecture profile: S=0.60*S_A+0.30*S_T+0.10*S_L, with S_A=clip(3500/(A+3000)), S_T=clip(ln(T/260416.66666666666)/ln(240)), S_L=clip((300-L)/237). All values below are commercial public previews using the fixed ASAP7 RVT/TT libraries; none is an official hidden grade. SQNR above 50 dB has no score bonus. The 500 um2, 62.5 M FFT/s and 63-cycle scales are aspirational anchors.

Mandatory contract: complete 64-point forward unscaled FFT, natural input/output, signed 16-bit input and 24-bit output with 15 fractional bits; each tested nonzero frame >=50 dB, exact zero frame; synchronous high reset aborts inflight work; 64 consecutive outputs, 384-cycle service, first output<=300 and last<=364, setup and hold at 10 ns.

## Initial competing hypotheses and numerical screens

- Folded radix2 with one shared butterfly minimizes arithmetic, but bank muxes and 192 compute cycles can lose throughput and latency credit.
- Two shared butterflies with four parity banks trade duplicated arithmetic for 96 compute cycles and shorter bank muxes.
- Streaming SDF can earn enough II/frequency credit to justify more storage and arithmetic; radix2-squared pairing and a single alternating reorder buffer may limit its area cost.

F001 used 20-bit Q13 storage and Q13 twiddles with truncation; numerical screen failed at 48.353385 dB. F002 rounded inputs/products and passed at 50.620292 dB, first/last256/319. Its complete area diagnostic passed mapped checks at 1767.56256 um2; no combined architecture score is claimed. F003 used two butterflies, four parity banks, Q14 data and Q11 twiddles. F004 replaced four real products by three exact products; area fell from 2213.14194 to 2108.98242 um2 but fixed-clock STA path estimate worsened from 3.6779 to 4.3187 ns. The diagnostic alone did not justify selecting F004; it has no full combined score.

S002 began natural-order reads 14 cycles sooner than S001. S003 reduced coefficient precision to 9 fractional bits. R001 paired radix2 stages into radix2-squared, removing two nontrivial complex multipliers. R002 tried half-up stage rounding at Q14->Q13->Q12 and passed at 51.304864 dB; R003 changed input and stage boundaries to nearest-even and passed at 53.254771 dB. R004 predecoded coefficients and registered three exact real products; numerical output stayed the same, with two added cycles. R005/C005 tested one-hot output memory reads. R006/C006 and R007/C007 quantized only final reorder storage to Q10 and Q11 respectively. The Q10 screen passed at 50.220814 dB; independent public-seed 8192-frame screens gave 50.284084 dB (Q10) and 51.954103 dB (Q11). These are public development inputs, not hidden evaluation data.

## Complete architecture measurements

| Candidate | Area um2 | Worst SQNR dB | Verified II | Certified ns | First / last cycles | Public score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| F003 | 2213.14194 | 56.361896 | 224 | 3.687255859 | 160 / 223 | 0.546015873 |
| S001 | 3125.50002 | 56.361896 | 64 | 2.935058594 | 139 / 202 | 0.575940406 |
| S003 | 3069.65862 | 55.758176 | 64 | 2.668457031 | 125 / 188 | 0.590214187 |

All full runs use 1024 independent random frames plus 192 directed frames, 1024-frame continuous mandatory service, all 321 integer IIs 64..384 with 1024 consecutive RTL frames each, representative mapped comparisons from initial modes 0, 1, 20261121, and fixed-netlist PrimeTime clock scans. The smallest passing II is independently measured. Failed optional intervals are not mandatory violations. Quick screens and area diagnostics are separate rows in measurements.csv and have no combined score.

## Weighted decisions

| Comparison | 0.60 delta area | 0.30 delta throughput | 0.10 delta latency | Delta total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| F003 -> S001 | -0.059998932 | +0.081062706 | +0.008860759 | +0.029924533 |

Choose the highest completed feasible combined preview, even when another candidate has lower area, more SQNR or shorter latency. All selected score components are below saturation; II 64 is already the lower boundary of the tested serial-interface range.

## Final implementation

Selected **C005**, score **0.672667356470**, resolved=true, score_valid=true, scoring_scope=public_preview, official_score=false. Mapped area 3023.221320002 um2; II 64; certified period 0.630859375000 ns; effective throughput 24767801.858 FFT/s; worst first/last 123/186 cycles. Minimum SQNR across all matching-source public runs is 53.254770813 dB. Zero-frame output is exact.

The final radix2-squared SDF pipeline has feedback depths 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 complex samples. For each paired group a=x0+x2, b=x1+x3, c=x0-x2, d=x1-x3: the first stage applies only exact -j to d; the second forms a+b, a-b, c-j*d, c+j*d in four quarters, followed by twiddle exponents 0, 2*j, j, 3*j. There are two nontrivial complex rotations. Each uses three exact real products with no intermediate quantization, registered coefficients/products, and one post-product quantization boundary.

Nearest-even Q15->Q14 at input, Q14->Q13 after stage 2 and Q13->Q12 after stage 4; 19-bit Q12 final reorder storage.
A guard bit is added at each butterfly. Twiddle factors have 9 fractional bits in signed 10-bit coefficients; unit and quarter rotations bypass multiplication exactly. Fixed-point representation shifts preserve external FFT gain. Products use half-up nearest rounding, while the explicitly named narrowing boundaries use nearest-even. No gate pruning or approximate arithmetic compressors are used.

Natural-order output uses one 64-word complex flop memory. Successive frames alternate sequential and bit-reversed write addresses; each following frame overwrites in the preceding read order, safely supporting II 64 without a second frame buffer. Since max(bit_reverse(k)-k)=49, the first read at offset 50 is safe and yields one 64-cycle output burst. All buffers, read/write muxes, coefficient logic and control are counted.

All state uses the specified positive-edge clock. Reset clears valid/start chains, counters and reorder state; data arrays need no reset because a fresh complete transaction overwrites each valid datum before use. Long idle gaps do not advance a free-running frame timer. All reset and gap tests passed.

## Synthesis and provenance

The custom DC recipe flattens hierarchy, sets a 0.5 ns synthesis target, fixes multiple-port nets, keeps the direct clock, runs compile_ultra with a timing request, then incremental hold repair. The installed DC reports its timing_high_effort_script flag as ignored; clock steering and legal mapping still produce the measured implementation. The 0.5 ns target is an optimization request, not a timing claim. Independent grading imports the structural netlist without recipe execution, applies the fixed 10 ns SDC and certifies the actual period above. Constraints, libraries, scorer and reference were never changed.

Authoritative public report: `runs/arch_C005/result.json`, copied byte-for-byte to `submission/public_verification.json`. Selection/report hashes are in `frozen_selection.json`. All experiments and source snapshots remain under `experiments/`; full measurements and per-component scores are in `measurements.csv`.

Reproduce with `bash run_synopsys_debug.sh submission --profile architecture --out runs/reproduce_final` from FFT-Bench. To regenerate the export with the matching recipe use `bash synopsys.sh build submission --export --out runs/rebuild_final`, then independently evaluate in a fresh output directory.

## Limits and stopping decision

Stopped after 9 completed architecture candidates plus numerical and area screens. The selected candidate has the highest complete feasible public score in this search. No global optimality or hidden-test acceptance is claimed. SQNR margin on the worst observed matching-source public frame is 3.254771 dB; this is finite empirical coverage. Timing/area are pre-layout ideal-interconnect measurements, not routed/silicon performance or power. Formal equivalence and P&R were not run; required multi-initial-state mapped simulation and STA passed. No private FFT-Eval resources, calibration or hidden inputs were accessed.

content.text:
Implemented and froze **C005** in [submission](/mnt/DATA1/sj/FFT/Codex-GPT-6.1-Sol-Max/FFT-Bench/submission), the best of **11 complete public architecture evaluations**.

**Public preview score: 0.672667 — `resolved=true`.**

| Metric | Measured result |
|---|---:|
| Mapped area | 3,023.22 μm² |
| Worst-frame SQNR | 53.25 dB |
| Verified II | 64 cycles |
| Certified period | 0.630859 ns |
| STA-derived throughput | 24.77 million FFT/s |
| First / last output | 123 / 186 cycles |

The design uses **R2²SDF**, two pipelined complex rotators with three real products each, and one alternating reorder buffer. Precision progresses through Q14 → Q13 → Q12 with nearest-even narrowing and nine fractional-bit twiddles. Synthesis uses DC `compile_ultra`, a 0.5 ns optimization target, and incremental hold repair.

The score improved from **0.546016** for the folded baseline. Mandatory checks, all **321 IIs × 1,024 frames**, and mapped comparisons from three initial states passed. Narrower reorder buffers produced worse combined scores and were rejected.

Matching RTL, recipe, mapped netlist, manifest, [design record](/mnt/DATA1/sj/FFT/Codex-GPT-6.1-Sol-Max/FFT-Bench/submission/DESIGN_PLAN.md), and [measurements](/mnt/DATA1/sj/FFT/Codex-GPT-6.1-Sol-Max/FFT-Bench/submission/measurements.csv) are included. These are pre-layout public results; hidden acceptance and post-route performance remain unverified.
